MB.title: Mystery Phone: Chat-Code Takeover
MB.brief: Sana's friend asked her for something unusual on Friday night. No leads this time. Review the device, find the red flags and reconstruct the attack.
MB.closing: A new device, a new story, the same five stages. You identified them without leads.

MB-M01.explain: This code is real, belongs to Sana, and says never to share it.
MB-01.explain: Meera always writes Sanu. When a friend’s account is stolen, the thief sounds slightly wrong.
MB-02.explain: No call, only text. A thief hides a voice that is not Meera’s.
MB-03.explain: A 2-minute timer stops Sana from calling Meera.

MB-G1.explain: The same sentence was sent to many people. A real friend would not copy and paste.
MB.fix.q: A friend’s account asks you to send back a code that came to your phone. What do you do?
MB.fix.a: Send it, since it is your friend.
MB.fix.a.why: The code is the key to your account.
MB.fix.b: Never share the code. Call your friend on a call and tell others.
MB.fix.b.why: Yes. Your codes are yours alone.
MB.debrief.mechanism: This is an account takeover chain. The attacker triggered a login code to the victim's number, then used a hijacked friend's account to ask the victim to forward it. The code authorises a login on the attacker's device. Writing style, refusing calls and a two-minute deadline were the tells.
MB.debrief.c1: A code sent to you is for you only. No friend ever needs it.
MB.debrief.c2: Confirm by a voice call, not by chat.
MB.debrief.c3: If your account is taken over, warn your contacts immediately.
MB-C08.explain: Meera's genuine messages call her Sanu. This is the baseline that exposes the impostor.
